correctness.rationale: Packing means selected closed neighborhoods pairwise disjoint, equivalently selected vertices pairwise graph distance at least 3; isolation means N[S] covers at least one endpoint of each edge. A 3-subdivision of any edge preserves a packing-isolating set: add q at the middle new vertex when neither endpoint selected, or r/p near the unselected endpoint when one is selected, retaining mutual distance>=3 and all-edge coverage. A finite base with 3<=a<=b<=8,0<=d<=10 comprises 231 triples; independent exhaustive edge-coverage DFS recomputed all 225 satisfiable cases and the precise six no-solution cases (not mere random samples). Repeated 3-subdivision of cycle/bridge edges lifts every larger triple from a nonexceptional base; large parameters reduce into [6,8] for cycles/[8,10] for bridges so cannot fall into a listed exception. The proof needs the exact finite base plus structural lemma, not extrapolation.

final_claim: Exactly six two-cycle cactus graphs B_(a,b,d), 3<=a<=b and d>=0, fail to admit a simultaneous packing-isolating set: (5,5,0),(5,5,1),(3,5,2),(5,5,3),(5,5,4),(5,5,7). Every other such graph has one.
